The *Upasīvamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 10) is a canonical commentary included in the *Cūḷaniddesa*, belonging to the late sutta strata of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It provides an exposition and word-by-word exegesis of the *Upasīvamāṇavapucchā* ("Questions of the Student Upasīva"), which forms part of the *Pārāyanavagga* in the *Sutta Nipāta* (Snp 5.7) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also notes its relationship to the introductory verses (*Pucchā*, Cnd 2) and records two translations across two languages [SuttaCentral].
SuttaCentral identifies passage-level parallels between this text and other Niddesa treatises, including the *Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa* (Cnd 23), *Mogharājamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 19), *Dhotakamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 9), *Sāriputtasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 16), and *Tuvaṭakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 14), as well as sections of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 1.1 *Ñāṇakathā* and Ps 1.4 *Indriyakathā*), with a resembling parallel in the *Purābhedasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 10) [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus registers extensive internal text reuse across the Pali canon, identifying 2,192 matches across 103 texts [DharmaNexus]. Its largest shared passages occur with neighboring commentaries in the *Cūḷaniddesa* and *Mahāniddesa*—most prominently the *Mettagūmāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 8), *Purābhedasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 10), *Nandamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 11), *Pucchā* (Cnd 2), and *Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa* (Cnd 23)—as well as the underlying root verses of Snp 5.7 [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali literature, DharmaNexus detects lower-scoring automatic alignments with Chinese texts, including portions of the *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26) and *Saṁyukta Āgama* (T 99) [DharmaNexus].
